05. Species reports and Quarto customization

Source: vignettes/species-reports.Rmd
species-reports.Rmd

Combined reports

Report functions combine existing accessors. They preserve each section’s format and rules, so users can start with a standard report and build a custom composition when they need control over its content or order.

The code chunks in this vignette are not executed when it is built: some require external services, while others require locally saved files. No credentials, user-specific file paths, or downloads are included.

Choosing a report

Function Sections Source considerations
sacha_clb_report() Accepted name, first publication, indexations, common names, classification, synonyms and combinations, documented areas, and references. ChecklistBank sections retain the configured web behavior.
sacha_spatial_report() Documented areas and a cropped GBIF map. language applies to the area text; additional arguments are passed to gbif_map_crop_md().
sacha_report() Name, first publication, images, indexations, common names, classification, synonymy, areas, GBIF map, and references. source = "local" is the default for images and maps; source = "web" requests both services online. ChecklistBank sections continue to use their web source.

For sacha_report(), source = "local" requires iNaturalist and GBIF files that match the species and filters. If the cropped map requires a boundary, provide one or configure it in advance. ChecklistBank sections may still query the web even when local files are used, so the report is not fully offline.

The _md reports emit document markup. In Quarto or R Markdown, results='asis' lets the renderer process that markup and its figures. Figure options and cross-references are covered in the maps and images vignettes.

Shared values and explicit arguments

sacha_arg_configure() sets shared arguments for subsequent calls. An argument supplied directly to a report takes precedence over its shared value. Each section’s arguments retain the meaning and accepted values of the underlying function; ?sacha_report lists the forwarded names, and the corresponding accessors document how to use them.

sacha_arg_configure(
  species = "Bidens andicola",
  number_observations = 1,
  image_size = "medium",
  source = "local"
)

sacha_report(crop_box = c(-180, -90, 180, 90, "Global extent"))
sacha_report(
  species = "Bidens andicola",
  source = "web",
  crop_box = c(-180, -90, 180, 90, "Global extent")
)

sacha_clear_cache()

The first report inherits the configured values. In the second, explicit arguments replace shared values with the same names. sacha_clear_cache() resets configuration and removes shared values, but does not delete saved files or reset iNaturalist download-volume and delay controls.

Advanced section composition

When the standard order does not fit a report’s purpose, Markdown accessors can be combined directly. For example, a species account can lead with classification, limit the images, include a full-extent map, and end with references. This approach also makes it possible to omit sections that are not relevant.

Custom compositions should account for source-specific behavior: source = "local" in iNaturalist and GBIF requires prepared files; ChecklistBank functions and locations() do not accept that argument and follow their own query rules. Each section is rendered in call order, so map and image calls should be placed in a chunk configured for asis output.

More focused outputs can be assembled without querying every module. For example, a nomenclatural note can combine a name, publication, synonyms, and references; a geographic account can pair locations_md() with gbif_map_crop_md(); and a photographic plate can use inat_images_md() without a map. Keep filters and parameters that affect record selection, licensing, or geographic scale explicit so the composition remains interpretable and reproducible.

Rendering practices

  • For repeated renders, use local sources for images and maps after validating and archiving the required files.
  • Avoid repeating online queries for each output format of the same book; retrieve or save the data once and reuse it.
  • Keep provenance metadata, dates, and licenses with downloaded files.
  • Use results='asis' in chunks that print Markdown generated by the package.
  • Define cross-references from the identifiers produced by the functions and confirm them in the rendered document.

ChecklistBank, GBIF, and iNaturalist policies and availability may change. Consult each provider’s documentation before planning large-scale retrieval or redistributing records and images.
